summary: A Medium blog post by Rakesh Rajpurohit explaining how Hugging Face Transformers integrates with the Bitsandbytes library to simplify model quantization. It defines quantization as reducing numerical precision to save memory and speed up execution, shows install steps, and gives code for loading models in 4-bit and 8-bit, plus advanced options such as compute dtype, NF4, nested quantization, CPU offloading, outlier threshold and module skipping.
one_line: A tutorial on using Hugging Face Transformers with Bitsandbytes to load and fine-tune quantized 4-bit and 8-bit language models.
key_facts: The blog post was written by Rakesh Rajpurohit and published on Aug 20, 2023, with a reading time of 4 min.
Quantization reduces the precision of numerical values, for example representing values as 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit floating-point numbers.
Quantization significantly reduces memory usage and can speed up model execution while maintaining acceptable accuracy.
Hugging Face's Transformers library has been integrated with the Bitsandbytes library to simplify model quantization.
Setting load_in_4bit=True in .from_pretrained can reduce memory usage by approximately fourfold.
Setting load_in_8bit=True in .from_pretrained reduces the memory footprint by approximately half.
The get_memory_footprint method can be called on a model to check its memory footprint.
Setting bnb_4bit_compute_dtype to a value such as torch.bfloat16 can change the compute data type and may improve speed in specific scenarios.
The NF4 data type is designed for weights initialized using a normal distribution and is enabled with bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4".
Nested quantization is enabled with bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True and is recommended for greater memory efficiency, especially when fine-tuning large models.
A quantized model loaded from the Hub can be loaded with from_pretrained without specifying load_in_8bit=True, but requires both Bitsandbytes and Accelerate installed.
Setting llm_int8_enable_fp32_cpu_offload=True allows distributing weights between CPU and GPU for fitting large models.
The llm_int8_threshold argument changes the outlier threshold and affects inference speed.
The llm_int8_skip_modules argument skips converting specific modules to 8-bit.
The example model used in the code is bigscience/bloom-1b7.
